conventions: לִפְנֵי is fused under rule 30 to whichever single English rendering the ASV writes for it in this chapter — 'with' (v.1), 'on' (v.2), 'were with' with the construction copula (v.3), 'before' (vv.15, 16, 23) — and in v.27 to the noun 'presence' standing after a separately written 'from' on the מִן; the margin's 'Hebrew before' is read and set aside each time (rule 38).

'went away' for a bare וַיֵּלַךְ (vv.11, 12): 'went' writes the whole of הָלַךְ and no מִן or other morpheme in the clause states the departure, so 'away' is its own `added` unit under rule 44's surplus-particle test. The competing reading keeps 'away' with the verb; the chapter takes the `added` reading in both verses.

The one-word question הֲשָׁלוֹם → 'Is all well' and its answer שָׁלוֹם → 'All is well' (vv.21, 22): the supplied subject 'all' is `added` under rule 20's closing sentence, the fronted 'Is' goes to הֲ under rule 20, and the 'is' of the answer joins the predicate noun.

Bare locative בֵּית רִמּוֹן (v.18, three times): after בּוֹא the supplied 'into' is the verb's under rule 44, since the place is what בּוֹא governs; after חוה the supplied 'in' belongs to the noun under rule 33, with the supplied 'the' on the construct under rule 29.

The italic 'himself' of 'dipped himself' (v.14) is kept with טָבַל as the ASV's rendering of the verb's intransitive use here, not marked `added` like the supplied object pronouns of vv.16, 23 and 24; the competing `added` reading is named in the unit note.
report: Checked every multi-treatment bucket in the candidate table and every `added` unit in the dump. No construction is analysed two ways without the source licensing the difference.

Recurring constructions are consistent: לִפְנֵי fuses to the single English rendering written for it in every occurrence (with / on / were with / before / presence); מֵאֵת and מֵעַל fuse headed on the first morpheme (vv.15, 19, 20, 21, 26); apodosis waws take 'that' where the ASV writes it (vv.7, 8) and go unrepresented where it writes nothing (vv.21, 24); interrogative הֲ takes the fronted copula or auxiliary in all six clauses; supplied object pronouns are `added` in vv.16, 23, 24; 'went away' marks 'away' added in both v.11 and v.12.
The one-word question/answer הֲשָׁלוֹם / שָׁלוֹם is read the same way in vv.21 and 22: supplied 'all' added, copula to the particle or to the predicate.

BSB disagreements are all documented convention differences (object markers, silent לְ/אֶל under rules 27 and 40, unrendered articles beside demonstratives and agreement articles, the resumptive suffix of 'before whom' in v.16 under rule 22, the unrendered positive-oath כִּי אִם in v.20, apodosis waws, the paragogic he in v.22). None is a genuine error.
